text:
Zara Bloom: Hi all  day 2 and hitting a wall. Running docker-compose for local dev (web, postgres, redis) on an M1 Mac. Postgres container repeatedly exits with permission errors trying to write PG_VERSION. Also my init SQLs in ./db/init never ran. Any quick checklist or who to DM?

Ken Ito: Welcome! Common on Macs: host bind-mounted pgdata with mismatched ownership. Quick test: stop compose, sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata && docker-compose up postgres. But better is a named volume so Docker manages FS perms.

Zara Bloom: Switched to a named volume and postgres starts, but my app running on host still can't talk to it unless I publish a port. I tried host.docker.internal:5432 but connection times out.

Alex Grey: If your machine already runs a system Postgres (brew), it may be binding 5432. `brew services list` then `brew services stop postgresql` if you can. Alternatively map to a high host port: `ports: - "15432:5432"` then use host.docker.internal:15432.

Ken Ito: On M1 also watch for image architecture issues. If the container exits with "exec format error" switch to arm64-friendly tags (e.g., postgres:15-alpine) or set `platform: linux/amd64` as a last resort.

Zara Bloom: Good tip, I did see an exec format error earlier. After stopping brew postgres and mapping 15432 it connects from the host. But my init script still didn't create the user/db. Logs show "Database directory appears to contain a database; Skipping initialization".

Alex Grey: That means the entrypoint found files at PGDATA and won't re-run init. Two possibilities: (1) your compose sets PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata but you mounted a volume to /var/lib/postgresql/data (path mismatch), or (2) the volume already had files. Fix by aligning mount to the PGDATA path or removing the volume: `docker-compose down -v` then `docker volume rm <name>` or `rm -rf ./pgdata/*` if using host bind. Recreate afterwards to trigger init scripts.

Zara Bloom: My compose had PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata but I mounted to /var/lib/postgresql/data  that explains it. One more: my SQL files were 0640 (editor default). Could that prevent the entrypoint from reading them?

Ken Ito: Yes, entrypoint runs as postgres user and needs those files readable. `chmod 644 ./db/init/*.sql` usually fixes it. Also ensure files have .sql or .sh extensions and are mounted into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` correctly (try `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro postgres:15 ls -l /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` to verify).

tooling-bot: Dev docs: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup includes recommended compose snippets, .env.local.template (gitignored), and Mac M1 tips such as using named volumes and 15xxx port namespace for host mappings.

Zara Bloom: Awesome, that unblocked me. I'll align mount+PGDATA, chmod the files, nuke the named volume and re-up. If still blocked I'll DM Ken. Thanks all!
